---
name: slack-api
description: Slack Web API automation: post and schedule messages, send DMs and thread replies, read channel history, list channels and members, manage reactions, upload and share files, search messages and files, and create, invite to, or archive channels. Use when the user asks to send, fetch, search, or manage content in a Slack workspace (for example, "post an update to the team channel", "summarize recent messages", "who is in #design", "upload this file to Slack", "invite Ada to #general"), or needs help choosing methods, scopes, pagination, or troubleshooting Slack API calls.
---

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the official Web API (`https://slack.com/api`): read and post messages, manage conversations, users, reactions, files, and search. All calls go through the bundled scripts, which read the token from the environment and print compact results.

## Quick Start

1. **Provide a token.** Export a bot token (starts with `xoxb-`) as `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`. Tokens must never be hardcoded into commands, scripts, or messages; read them from the environment only.
   The app must be installed in the target workspace with the OAuth scopes the task needs (see `references/api.md`).

2. **Verify connectivity and identity** (no scopes required):
   ```bash
   node scripts/slack.cjs auth.test
   ```

3. **Send a message** (`chat:write`):
   ```bash
   node scripts/slack.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C0123456789","text":"Hello from an agent"}'
   ```

4. **Read the last messages** of a channel (`channels:history`):
   ```bash
   node scripts/slack.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C0123456789","limit":10}'
   ```

## Method Picker

| Task | Method(s) / script | Typical scope(s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send a message | `chat.postMessage` | `chat:write` |
| Reply inside a thread | `chat.postMessage` with `thread_ts` | `chat:write` |
| Show a message only to one user | `chat.postEphemeral` (add `user`) | `chat:write` |
| Edit / delete your app's message | `chat.update` / `chat.delete` | `chat:write` |
| Schedule a message | `chat.scheduleMessage` (add `post_at`) | `chat:write` |
| List channels / DMs | `conversations.list` (types: `public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im`) | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` |
| Channel history | `conversations.history` | `channels:history` (or `groups/im/mpim:history`) |
| Thread replies | `conversations.replies` (add `ts` of the parent) | `channels:history` |
| Who is in a channel | `conversations.members` | `channels:read` |
| Open / start a DM | `conversations.open` (then `chat.postMessage`) | `im:write` (see reference) |
| Create / invite / rename / archive | `conversations.create` / `.invite` / `.rename` / `.archive` | `channels:manage` (public) or `groups:write` (private) |
| Find a user | `users.lookupByEmail` / `users.info` / `users.list` | `users:read` (+ `users:read.email` for emails) |
| Add / remove a reaction | `reactions.add` / `reactions.remove` | `reactions:write` |
| Search | `search.messages` / `search.files` | `search:read` |
| Upload and share a file | `scripts/upload_file.cjs <file> <channel>` | `files:write` |
| Verify token / app | `auth.test` | none (app must be installed) |

Read `references/api.md` for the full catalog with parameters, examples, scopes, error codes, and formatting rules.

## Core Workflow

1. **Choose the method** from the picker above or the catalog in `references/api.md`.
2. **Resolve identifiers to IDs.** Slack APIs take encoded IDs (`C…` channel, `U…` user, `D…` DM, `G…` group). Do not guess: list channels with `conversations.list` (match `name`), look users up with `users.lookupByEmail`, and open DMs with `conversations.open` to obtain a `channel.id`.
3. **Call the method:**
   ```bash
   node scripts/slack.cjs <method> '<json-args>' [--pages N]
   ```
   The second argument is a JSON object of the method's parameters.
4. **Inspect the result.** `ok: true` means success; use the returned `ts`/`channel` for follow-ups. `ok: false` means the call failed; the `error` field (plus `needed`/`provided` scopes for `missing_scope`) tells you what to fix.
5. **Paginate when needed.** List endpoints return a `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Rerun with `--pages N` (default `1`) to follow the cursor for up to N requests total. Output is truncated at 400 lines by default; add `--full` to print everything.

## Working with Results

- **Timestamps** (`ts`) are epoch seconds with microseconds, e.g. `"1625250674.000100"`. Convert with `new Date(Number(ts) * 1000)`.
- **Threads:** replying to a message requires passing its `ts` as `thread_ts`. Without `thread_ts`, a reply starts a new top-level message. `conversations.replies` returns the parent as the first item.
- **History order:** `conversations.history` returns messages newest first; combine `oldest`/`latest` (epoch seconds or `ts`) with `inclusive: true` to bound the window.
- **Dry runs:** test in a low-noise channel you control, or use `chat.postEphemeral` so only a chosen user sees the result. Never run destructive calls (`chat.delete`, `conversations.archive`) without confirmation.
- **Deleting/editing:** a bot token can only `chat.update`/`chat.delete` messages its own app posted.
- **Message size:** the `text` field is limited to 40,000 characters; pass large payloads as `blocks` and keep them reasonable.

## Files in This Skill

- `scripts/slack.cjs` — generic caller: `node scripts/slack.cjs <method> '<json>' [--pages N] [--full]`. Reads `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` (fallback `SLACK_TOKEN`, `SLACK_OAUTH_TOKEN`); `SLACK_API_BASE_URL` overrides the base URL (default `https://slack.com/api`). Requires Node.js 18+ (global `fetch`). Prints a `Failure:` line and exits non-zero on errors, never a stack trace.
- `scripts/upload_file.cjs` — uploads a local file with the current upload flow: `node scripts/upload_file.cjs <file> [channel] [--comment text] [--thread-ts TS]`. Options: `--title NAME`, `--alt-text TEXT`.
- `references/api.md` — method catalog (parameters, scopes, examples), mrkdwn formatting, pagination, rate limits, and the error-code catalog. Read it when you need parameter details, need to pick a scope, hit an error code, or are formatting text. Grep for keywords such as `upload`, `thread`, `rate`, or a specific error code.

## Rules

- Never print, log, or commit tokens. Pass them only via environment variables.
- Prefer a bot token (`xoxb-`); reach for a user token (`xoxp-`) only when a task genuinely needs user-level permissions.
- Slack can change API details; when in doubt check the official method docs at `https://api.slack.com/methods/<method>`. When Slack rejects a call, `missing_scope` names the exact scope to add in the app configuration.

# Slack Web API Reference

Reference for interacting with `https://slack.com/api` using the bundled scripts (`scripts/slack.cjs`, `scripts/upload_file.cjs`) or raw HTTP.

## Contents

- [Authentication and Tokens](#authentication-and-tokens)
- [Method Catalog](#method-catalog)
  - [Messages](#messages)
  - [Conversations and Channels](#conversations-and-channels)
  - [Users](#users)
  - [Reactions](#reactions)
  - [Search](#search)
  - [Files and Uploads](#files-and-uploads)
  - [Utility](#utility)
- [Formatting Message Text](#formatting-message-text)
- [Resolving Names and IDs](#resolving-names-and-ids)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Rate Limits](#rate-limits)
- [Error Codes](#error-codes)

## Authentication and Tokens

- Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (the bundled scripts add it automatically).
- Token types: bot token `xoxb-…` (recommended), user token `xoxp-…`, app-level token `xapp-…` (not used by these scripts).
- The app must be installed in the workspace **with the OAuth scopes the task needs**. Scopes are granted per app, not per token; when a call fails with `missing_scope`, Slack returns the exact `needed` scope in the error body. Add it under App Settings → OAuth & Permissions, then reinstall.
- `auth.test` verifies a token and reports which workspace, team, user, and app it belongs to — always call it first when something looks wrong.
- Only `api.test` works without any token.

## Method Catalog

Examples assume `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` is set and use the bundled script:

```bash
node scripts/slack.cjs <method> '<json-args>'
```

All methods take a JSON object of parameters. Required parameters are marked **required**.

### Messages

**`chat.postMessage`** — scope `chat:write`. Send a message.
Params: `channel` **required** (channel/DM ID, see resolving below), `text`, `blocks` (rich layout; recommended over long text), `thread_ts` (reply inside that thread), `mrkdwn` (default true), `link_names` (`1` to linkify channel/user names), `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`, `reply_broadcast`.
Returns `channel`, `ts`, and `message`.
```bash
node scripts/slack.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C0123456789","text":"Ship it :rocket:","thread_ts":"1625250674.000100"}'
```

**`chat.postEphemeral`** — scope `chat:write`. Post a message only a specific `user` (required) sees, in `channel` (required). Same text/block options. Useful for silent tests and private results.

**`chat.update`** — scope `chat:write`. Edit an existing message: `channel` **required**, `ts` **required** (the message to edit), plus new `text`/`blocks`. A bot token can only edit messages its own app posted.

**`chat.delete`** — scope `chat:write`. Delete a message: `channel` **required**, `ts` **required**. A bot token can only delete messages its own app posted; deleting arbitrary messages requires appropriate user/admin permissions. Destructive: confirm before running.

**`chat.scheduleMessage`** — scope `chat:write`. Schedule `channel`/`text`/`blocks` with `post_at` (future Unix timestamp, at most ~120 days out). Returns `scheduled_message_id`; cancel with `chat.deleteScheduledMessage` (`channel` + `scheduled_message_id`).

### Conversations and Channels

**`conversations.list`** — read scopes by type (`channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`). List conversations the app can see.
Params: `types` (comma list; default `public_channel`; add `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im` as needed), `limit` (default 100, max 200), `cursor`, `exclude_archived` (`true`).
Returns `channels[]` with `id`, `name`, `is_archived`, `is_private`, `is_member`, `is_im`, `user` (for DMs).

**`conversations.info`** — same read scopes. One conversation: `channel` **required**. Returns `channel` with full metadata.

**`conversations.history`** — history scope for the conversation type (`channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history`). Read messages.
Params: `channel` **required**, `limit` (default 100, max 999), `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` (epoch seconds or `ts` strings; use `inclusive: true` to include the boundary messages), `include_all_metadata`.
Returns `messages[]` **newest first** (each with `ts`, `user`, `type`, `text`, `blocks`, `thread_ts` when inside a thread), plus `has_more`.

**`conversations.replies`** — same history scopes. Read a thread: `channel` **required** and `ts` **required** (parent message ts). Returns the whole thread, parent first.

**`conversations.members`** — read scope (`channels:read`, etc.). List member user IDs of a conversation: `channel` **required**. Paginated like list endpoints.

**`conversations.open`** — open a DM (or MPIM) and get its `channel.id`. Params: `users` **required** (comma-separated user IDs; one for DM, several for group DM), `return_channel` (`true` to get full channel object).
Scope note: the required scope depends on the conversation kind (`im:write` for DMs, `mpim:write` for group DMs, `channels:manage`/`groups:write` for opening an existing channel). If `im:write` is unavailable, find an existing DM instead via `conversations.list '{"types":"im"}'` and match on the `user` field.

**`conversations.create`** — scope `channels:manage` (public) or `groups:write` (private). Params: `name` **required**, `is_private` (`true`). Returns the new `channel`.

**`conversations.invite`** — scope `channels:manage` (public) or `groups:write` (private). Add members: `channel` **required**, `users` **required** (comma-separated IDs, up to ~1,000 per call). Returns the channel; inviting to a private channel requires the inviter to be a member.

**`conversations.rename`** — scope `channels:manage` (public) or `groups:write` (private). `channel` **required**, `name` **required**.

**`conversations.archive`** / **`conversations.unarchive`** — scopes as above. `channel` **required**. Archiving hides the channel from the general list; it is not deletion. Destructive-ish: confirm before running.

**`conversations.setTopic`** / **`conversations.setPurpose`** — scopes as above. `channel` **required**, `topic`/`purpose` **required**.

### Users

**`users.lookupByEmail`** — scope `users:read` (+ `users:read.email` to see the address). `email` **required**. Returns the user object with `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile`.

**`users.info`** — scope `users:read` (+ `users:read.email`). `user` **required** (ID).

**`users.list`** — scope `users:read`. List workspace users. `limit` (default 100, max 200), `cursor`. Returns `members[]`; filter on `is_bot`/`deleted` as needed.

**`users.conversations`** — read scopes by type. List conversations a user (default: the authed user) is in: `user`, `types`, paginated. Slower to page; prefer `conversations.members` per channel when you only need one channel.

### Reactions

**`reactions.add`** — scope `reactions:write`. Params: `channel` **required**, `name` **required** (emoji name without colons, e.g. `+1`), `ts` **required** (target message).

**`reactions.remove`** — scope `reactions:write`. Same params.

**`reactions.get`** — scope `reactions:read`. `channel` **required**, `ts` **required**. Returns `reactions[]` on the message.

**`reactions.list`** — scope `reactions:read`. Reactions by a user (`user`, default authed user), paginated.

### Search

**`search.messages`** — scope `search:read`. Full-text search: `query` **required** (supports operators such as `in:#channel`, `from:@user`, `after:2023-01-01`, quoted phrases). `count` (default 20, max 100). Returns `messages.matches[]`, each with `channel`, `ts`, `user`, `text`, `blocks`.

**`search.files`** / **`search.all`** — scope `search:read`. Same `query` semantics for files or everything at once.

### Files and Uploads

The current upload flow has three steps (the legacy `files.upload` endpoint still exists but should not be used for new work):

1. **`files.getUploadURLExternal`** — scope `files:write`. Params: `filename` **required**, `length` **required** (byte count of the file), `alt_txt`, `snippet_type`. Returns `upload_url` and `file_id`.
2. **PUT** the raw file bytes to `upload_url` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. The upload URL is a temporary, signed, different host — do not POST JSON to it.
3. **`files.completeUploadExternal`** — scope `files:write`. Params: `files` **required** (`[{"id":"F…"}]` from step 1), `channel_id` (to share into a conversation), `initial_comment`, `thread_ts`. Returns `files[]` and, when shared into a channel, the message `channel`/`ts`.

`scripts/upload_file.cjs` automates all three steps from a local path:
```bash
node scripts/upload_file.cjs ./report.pdf C0123456789 --comment "Q3 numbers" --title "Q3 Report"
```
Equivalent raw sequence (for one-off or non-Node environments):
```bash
UP=$(curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"filename\":\"report.pdf\",\"length\":$(stat -f%z report.pdf)}" \
  https://slack.com/api/files.getUploadURLExternal)
# parse upload_url and file_id from UP, then:
curl -s -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @report.pdf "<upload_url>"
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"files":[{"id":"<file_id>"}],"channel_id":"C0123456789","initial_comment":"Q3 numbers"}' \
  https://slack.com/api/files.completeUploadExternal
```
Other file methods: `files.info` (`file`, scope `files:read`), `files.delete` (scope `files:write`, destructive), `files.sharedPublicURL` (scope `files:write`).

### Utility

- **`api.test`** — no token, no auth. Echo test: always callable.
- **`auth.test`** — verifies the token; returns `team`, `team_id`, `user`, `user_id`, `url`, and bot info when applicable.
- **`team.info`** — scope `team:read`. Workspace metadata (`team_id`, `name`, `domain`).
- **`team.billableInfo`** — scope `users:read`/`team:read`; rarely needed.

## Formatting Message Text

Slack uses a lightweight markup called mrkdwn in `text` fields (enabled by default):

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strikethrough~`, `` `code` ``, ``` ``preformatted`` ```, `>quote`
- Mentions: `<@U123456>` (user), `<#C123456>` (channel) — use IDs, not names
- Links: `<https://example.com/page|friendly label>`; bare URLs are linked automatically unless disabled
- Emoji: `:wave:`, `:+1:`, custom workspace emoji also by `:name:`
- Text is limited to 40,000 characters; keep request bodies under ~300 KB

For layout (headers, fields, buttons, dividers, images) use `blocks` (Block Kit) instead of long text:

```json
{
  "channel": "C0123456789",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Deploy finished* in 42s" } },
    { "type": "divider" },
    { "type": "context", "elements": [ { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Run by <@U123456>" } ] }
  ]
}
```

Block reference: `https://api.slack.com/reference/block-kit/blocks`. Interactive elements (buttons, selects) require handling interactive events / `views.open` for modals; static content works everywhere.

## Resolving Names and IDs

Slack Web API methods take encoded IDs; app tokens generally cannot send to a channel by its `#name`. Resolution recipes:

- **Channel by name:** `conversations.list` with `types: "public_channel,private_channel"` and `limit: 200`, page with `--pages`, then match `name === "#general".slice(1)`.
- **DM by user:** `conversations.open '{"users":"U…","return_channel":true}'` → `channel.id` (starts with `D`).
- **User by email:** `users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'` → `user.id` (starts with `U`).
- **Parent message for threads:** take `ts` from the message in `conversations.history` or from the `ts` returned by `chat.postMessage`.

## Pagination

Cursor-based pagination is the norm: responses with more data return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Send it back as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

- `scripts/slack.cjs` follows the cursor automatically when you pass `--pages N` (it merges array results and reports `pagesUsed`).
- Practical per-page `limit` maxima: `conversations.list`/`users.list` 200; `conversations.history` 999; search `count` 100.
- To fetch everything, loop until `next_cursor` is empty — but cap the number of pages to stay inside rate limits (see below).

## Rate Limits

- Slack applies per-method tiers; hitting a limit returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds) and/or `error: "rate_limited"`. Back off for the requested duration before retrying.
- When a method family is over-used, Slack may also throttle with secondary rate-limit headers; slow down rather than hammering.
- Practical guidance: keep polling loops small, cache lookups (channel/user IDs) instead of re-listing, and add small sleeps between bulk operations.
- Tier details live at `https://api.slack.com/docs/rate-limits`; they change, so do not hardcode numeric tiers.

## Error Codes

Every failure response is `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>", ...}` — often with HTTP 200, so always check `ok`. The bundled script prints `Failure: Slack API error: <code>` and exits non-zero. Common codes:

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token rejected | Check the token value; reinstall the app |
| `account_inactive` / `token_revoked` | Token no longer valid | Generate/install a fresh token |
| `missing_scope` | App lacks a scope | Error body includes `needed`; add it to the app and reinstall |
| `no_permission` | Token type not allowed for the action | Use a user token or different app |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad/unknown channel ID | Resolve the ID again via `conversations.list` |
| `not_in_channel` | App/user not a member | `conversations.join`/`invite` first (public) |
| `is_archived` | Channel archived | Unarchive before posting |
| `name_taken` / `invalid_name` | Channel name problem | Pick another name; 1–80 lowercase chars, no spaces |
| `user_not_found` | Bad user ID or not visible to the app | Check `users.lookupByEmail` result |
| `message_too_long` | Text over the limit | Shorten text or move content into `blocks` |
| `invalid_timestamp` | `ts` malformed/unknown | Use the exact `ts` string returned by Slack |
| `already_reacted` / `no_reaction` | Reaction state mismatch | Check current reactions with `reactions.get` |
| `file_not_found` | Bad file ID | Verify `file_id` from the upload step |
| `too_many_requests` / HTTP 429 | Rate limited | Honor `Retry-After`, then retry |
| `internal_error` | Slack-side failure | Retry after a short delay |
| `restricted_action` | Enterprise/org policy blocked it | Adjust org settings or use an admin-approved flow |
| `access_denied` | Org/enterprise policy | Usually requires an admin's approval workflow |

When a call fails, read the full error body: Slack often includes extra context such as `needed`, `provided`, or an `errors` map naming the offending parameter. Official method docs: `https://api.slack.com/methods/<method>`.

# Slack API

## Overview

Enable agent-driven Slack automation against the Slack Web API. All calls are HTTPS requests to `https://slack.com/api/<method>` and return a JSON envelope. Everything below works with `curl` or Python 3 stdlib (`urllib`); no SDK is required, though using one is fine when the environment already provides it.

## Authentication

   - Bot token `xoxb-...` (normal case) in the `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable.
   - User token `xoxp-...` only when the task explicitly requires user-scoped access (e.g., `search.messages`).
2. Send every request with an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
3. Never log, print, or hard-code tokens.

### Response envelope

Every method returns JSON: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success or `{"ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found"}` on failure. Always check `ok` and surface `error` before acting on payload fields.

Sanity-check credentials first:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  https://slack.com/api/auth.test
# -> {"ok":true,"url":"...","team":"...","user":"...","team_id":"T...","user_id":"U..."}
```

## Calling Convention

Minimal Python helper (stdlib only):

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

TOKEN = os.environ["SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"]

def slack(method, **payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"https://slack.com/api/{method}",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
                 "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        return json.load(resp)

result = slack("auth.test")
assert result.get("ok"), result.get("error")
```

Equivalent curl pattern:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from automation"}'
```

## Sending Messages

### Post a message — `chat.postMessage`

Pass `channel` (an ID, never a bare name; see "Resolving Names"), `text`, and optionally `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn`.

```python
r = slack("chat.postMessage",
          channel="C1234567890",
          text="Deploy finished: <https://ci.example.com/build/42|build 42> is green.")
assert r["ok"], r.get("error")
ts = r["ts"]          # message id; store it to update/delete/reply/react later
channel = r["channel"]
```

Success returns `ts` (the message id) and the `channel` the message landed in.

### Reply in a thread

Reuse the parent's `ts` as `thread_ts`. Replies must still target the parent's `channel`:

```python
slack("chat.postMessage",
      channel="C1234567890",
      thread_ts="1614892152.000500",
      text="Adding details to the thread.")
```

### Post ephemeral — `chat.postEphemeral`

Visible only to one user; requires `user` (a `U...` id) plus `channel`:

```python
slack("chat.postEphemeral",
      channel="C1234567890",
      user="U1234567890",
      text="Only you can see this.")
```

### Update / delete — `chat.update`, `chat.delete`

Identify the message by `channel` + `ts` (never by matching text):

```python
slack("chat.update", channel="C1234567890", ts=ts, text="Revised text.")
slack("chat.delete", channel="C1234567890", ts=ts)
```

### Blocks and mrkdwn

Prefer `blocks` for rich messages; `text` still supplies the fallback/notification preview.

- mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, ```preformatted```, `~strike~`.
- Links: `<https://example.com|click here>`.
- Mentions: `<@U1234567890>` for users, `<#C1234567890>` for channels.
- Blocks payload with user mention and formatted text:

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "text": "Build failed",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn",
      "text": "*Build 42 failed* — see <https://ci.example.com/logs/42|logs>. cc <@U1234567890>"}},
    {"type": "divider"},
    {"type": "actions", "elements": [
      {"type": "button", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Retry"},
       "value": "retry_42", "action_id": "retry"}
    ]}
  ]
}
```

Limits: at most 50 blocks; each block `text` field at most 3000 chars; plain `text` at most 40,000 chars. Exceeding them returns `invalid_blocks` or `msg_too_long`.

## Reading Conversations

Prefer the unified `conversations.*` methods over the deprecated `channels.*`, `groups.*`, `im.*`, and `mpim.*` method families (those still exist for legacy read-only edge cases, but are not needed for list/history).

### List conversations — `conversations.list`

Filter with `types` (comma-separated: `public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im`) and pass `exclude_archived=true` unless archives are wanted. Results are paginated — never assume one page returns everything (see Pagination).

```python
def list_conversations(types="public_channel,private_channel"):
    out, cursor = [], ""
    while True:
        page = slack("conversations.list",
                     types=types, exclude_archived=True, limit=200, cursor=cursor)
        assert page["ok"], page.get("error")
        out += page["channels"]
        cursor = (page.get("response_metadata") or {}).get("next_cursor", "")
        if not cursor:
            return out
```

### Open a DM or private channel — `conversations.open`

`conversations.open` with `users` (comma-separated user ids for a DM) returns the conversation `channel.id` (`D...` for a 1:1 DM). Posting to a DM channel without first opening it fails.

### Read history — `conversations.history`

`channel` is required; `limit` (1–999), `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` are epoch-seconds (or message `ts`) filters, `inclusive` controls whether the boundary message is included. Returns newest-first `messages`.

```python
page = slack("conversations.history", channel="C1234567890", limit=100)
assert page["ok"], page.get("error")
for m in page["messages"]:
    print(m.get("ts"), m.get("user"), m.get("text"))
```

### Read a thread — `conversations.replies`

Pass `channel` and the parent `ts` to fetch the whole thread including the parent message.

### Resolving Names to IDs

Use IDs everywhere in API calls; resolve a human-supplied channel/user name only when necessary:

1. Channel name → ID: paginate `conversations.list` with `types=public_channel,private_channel` and match `name` (case-insensitive). Prefix `#` from the user input is not part of `name`.
2. User → ID: `users.lookupByEmail` when an email is known; otherwise paginate `users.list` and match `name` or `profile.display_name`.
3. If the ID is not found, report `channel_not_found` / `user_not_found` style errors instead of guessing.

## Users

- `users.list` — paginated (limit up to 200); each member has `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.display_name`, `profile.email` (email only when the `users:read.email` scope is present).
- `users.lookupByEmail` — fastest way to map an email to a `U...` id; requires `users:read.email`.
- `users.info` — one user by `user` id.

## Uploading Files

`files.upload` is deprecated (removal planned for 2025); use the two-step upload API:

1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename`, `length` (byte count), optional `alt_txt`, `snippet_type` → returns `upload_url` and `file_id`.
2. `PUT` the raw file bytes to `upload_url` (no Slack auth header required on this URL).
3. `files.completeUploadExternal` with `files: [{"id": file_id, "title": filename}]` → returns the `file` object. Pass `channel_id` (and optional `thread_ts`) on this final call to share the file into a conversation.

```python
import os, urllib.request

data = open("report.pdf", "rb").read()
meta = slack("files.getUploadURLExternal",
             filename="report.pdf", length=len(data), alt_txt="Monthly report")
assert meta["ok"], meta.get("error")

put = urllib.request.Request(meta["upload_url"], data=data, method="PUT")
with urllib.request.urlopen(put) as resp:
    assert resp.status in (200, 201), resp.status

done = slack("files.completeUploadExternal",
             files=[{"id": meta["file_id"], "title": "report.pdf"}],
             channel_id="C1234567890")
assert done["ok"], done.get("error")
```

## Reactions

```python
slack("reactions.add", channel="C1234567890", name="white_check_mark", timestamp=ts)
slack("reactions.remove", channel="C1234567890", name="x", timestamp=ts)
```

Pass emoji names without surrounding colons. To react inside a thread, `timestamp` is the target message's `ts`.

## Search

`search.messages` is the only practical way to search across channels, but bot tokens are not granted the `search:read` scope — it requires a user token (`xoxp-...`). If only a bot token is available, say so rather than pretending search works, and offer to scan specific channels with `conversations.history` instead.

## Pagination Pattern

List-style methods (`conversations.list`, `conversations.history`, `users.list`, `search.messages`, ...) page with `cursor` + `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Loop until `next_cursor` is empty or absent; never assume the first page is the whole result.

```python
def paginate(method, items_key, **params):
    params.setdefault("limit", 200)
    params.setdefault("cursor", "")
    while True:
        page = slack(method, **params)
        assert page["ok"], page.get("error")
        for item in page.get(items_key, []):
            yield item
        nxt = (page.get("response_metadata") or {}).get("next_cursor", "")
        if not nxt:
            break
        params["cursor"] = nxt

channels = list(paginate("conversations.list", "channels",
                         types="public_channel", exclude_archived=True))
```

## Errors, Rate Limits, and Retries

- `ok: false` responses carry a machine-readable `error`. Common codes:

  | error | meaning / fix |
  |---|---|
  | `not_authed`, `invalid_auth`, `account_inactive`, `token_revoked` | token missing, wrong, or disabled |
  | `missing_scope`, `no_permission`, `restricted_action` | app lacks the scope/permission for this method |
  | `channel_not_found` | unknown channel id, or the app is not a member of a private channel |
  | `user_not_found` | unknown user id |
  | `is_archived` | target channel is archived |
  | `name_taken` | conversation name already in use |
  | `msg_too_long`, `invalid_blocks` | payload exceeds message limits |
  | `ratelimited`, HTTP 429 | slow down; obey `Retry-After` |
  | `internal_error`, HTTP 5xx | transient; retry with backoff |

- On HTTP 429 read the `Retry-After` header (seconds) and wait that long before retrying.
- On HTTP 5xx or network failure, retry with exponential backoff and jitter (e.g., 1s, 2s, 4s... capped).
- Be careful retrying writes: a timed-out `chat.postMessage` may still have been delivered, so a blind retry can duplicate a message. If a write times out without a response, prefer verifying via history or reporting the uncertainty over immediate re-send.

## Scopes and Token Setup

Create an app at `https://api.slack.com/apps` → OAuth & Permissions → add Bot Token Scopes → Install to Workspace → copy the Bot User OAuth Token (`xoxb-...`) into `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`.

Common bot scopes:

- `chat:write` — send/update/delete messages, ephemeral messages, threads.
- `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` — read message history in each conversation type.
- `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`, `channels:manage` — conversation metadata; create/archive/manage.
- `users:read`, `users:read.email` — list users and read emails.
- `files:write`, `files:read` — upload and read files.
- `reactions:write`, `reactions:read` — add/remove/read reactions.
- `team:read` — workspace metadata when needed.

## Working Guidelines

- Always address conversations, users, and messages by ID (`C...`, `D...`, `G...`, `U...`, `ts`). Resolve human-supplied names once, then reuse the IDs.
- Always paginate list endpoints; one page is not the full dataset.
- Use `conversations.*` methods; avoid deprecated legacy methods (`channels.list`, `im.list`, ...) unless a task explicitly requires them.
- The app must be a member of a private channel to read or post to it (`conversations.join` covers public channels only; for private ones the app must be invited or added via `conversations.invite` with `channels:manage`).
- Posting to a DM usually requires `conversations.open` first.
- Treat `ts` values as opaque message ids (strings like `"1614892152.000500"`). For `oldest`/`latest` filters you may pass the `ts` string or epoch-seconds (float or string).
- Sending to an archived channel fails with `is_archived`; tell the user and ask before unarchiving.
- If a request needs a scope the configured token lacks, report the exact `missing_scope` error and the scope name; do not silently degrade.

## Core Workflow

1. **Choose the method** from the picker above or the catalog in `references/api.md`.
2. **Resolve identifiers to IDs.** Slack APIs take encoded IDs (`C…` channel, `U…` user, `D…` DM, `G…` group). Do not guess: list channels with `conversations.list` (match `name`), look users up with `users.lookupByEmail`, and open DMs with `conversations.open` to obtain a `channel.id`.
3. **Call the method:**
   ```bash
   node scripts/slack.cjs <method> '<json-args>' [--pages N]
   ```
   The second argument is a JSON object of the method's parameters.
4. **Inspect the result.** `ok: true` means success; use the returned `ts`/`channel` for follow-ups. `ok: false` means the call failed; the `error` field (plus `needed`/`provided` scopes for `missing_scope`) tells you what to fix.
5. **Paginate when needed.** List endpoints return a `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Rerun with `--pages N` (default `1`) to follow the cursor for up to N requests total. Output is truncated at 400 lines by default; add `--full` to print everything.

## Working with Results

- **Timestamps** (`ts`) are epoch seconds with microseconds, e.g. `"1625250674.000100"`. Convert with `new Date(Number(ts) * 1000)`.
- **Threads:** replying to a message requires passing its `ts` as `thread_ts`. Without `thread_ts`, a reply starts a new top-level message. `conversations.replies` returns the parent as the first item.
- **History order:** `conversations.history` returns messages newest first; combine `oldest`/`latest` (epoch seconds or `ts`) with `inclusive: true` to bound the window.
- **Dry runs:** test in a low-noise channel you control, or use `chat.postEphemeral` so only a chosen user sees the result. Never run destructive calls (`chat.delete`, `conversations.archive`) without confirmation.
- **Deleting/editing:** a bot token can only `chat.update`/`chat.delete` messages its own app posted.
- **Message size:** the `text` field is limited to 40,000 characters; pass large payloads as `blocks` and keep them reasonable.

## Method Catalog

Examples assume `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` is set and use the bundled script:

```bash
node scripts/slack.cjs <method> '<json-args>'
```

All methods take a JSON object of parameters. Required parameters are marked **required**.

### Messages

**`chat.postMessage`** — scope `chat:write`. Send a message.
Params: `channel` **required** (channel/DM ID, see resolving below), `text`, `blocks` (rich layout; recommended over long text), `thread_ts` (reply inside that thread), `mrkdwn` (default true), `link_names` (`1` to linkify channel/user names), `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`, `reply_broadcast`.
Returns `channel`, `ts`, and `message`.
```bash
node scripts/slack.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C0123456789","text":"Ship it :rocket:","thread_ts":"1625250674.000100"}'
```

**`chat.postEphemeral`** — scope `chat:write`. Post a message only a specific `user` (required) sees, in `channel` (required). Same text/block options. Useful for silent tests and private results.

**`chat.update`** — scope `chat:write`. Edit an existing message: `channel` **required**, `ts` **required** (the message to edit), plus new `text`/`blocks`. A bot token can only edit messages its own app posted.

**`chat.delete`** — scope `chat:write`. Delete a message: `channel` **required**, `ts` **required**. A bot token can only delete messages its own app posted; deleting arbitrary messages requires appropriate user/admin permissions. Destructive: confirm before running.

**`chat.scheduleMessage`** — scope `chat:write`. Schedule `channel`/`text`/`blocks` with `post_at` (future Unix timestamp, at most ~120 days out). Returns `scheduled_message_id`; cancel with `chat.deleteScheduledMessage` (`channel` + `scheduled_message_id`).

### Conversations and Channels

**`conversations.list`** — read scopes by type (`channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`). List conversations the app can see.
Params: `types` (comma list; default `public_channel`; add `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im` as needed), `limit` (default 100, max 200), `cursor`, `exclude_archived` (`true`).
Returns `channels[]` with `id`, `name`, `is_archived`, `is_private`, `is_member`, `is_im`, `user` (for DMs).

**`conversations.info`** — same read scopes. One conversation: `channel` **required**. Returns `channel` with full metadata.

**`conversations.history`** — history scope for the conversation type (`channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history`). Read messages.
Params: `channel` **required**, `limit` (default 100, max 999), `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` (epoch seconds or `ts` strings; use `inclusive: true` to include the boundary messages), `include_all_metadata`.
Returns `messages[]` **newest first** (each with `ts`, `user`, `type`, `text`, `blocks`, `thread_ts` when inside a thread), plus `has_more`.

**`conversations.replies`** — same history scopes. Read a thread: `channel` **required** and `ts` **required** (parent message ts). Returns the whole thread, parent first.

**`conversations.members`** — read scope (`channels:read`, etc.). List member user IDs of a conversation: `channel` **required**. Paginated like list endpoints.

**`conversations.open`** — open a DM (or MPIM) and get its `channel.id`. Params: `users` **required** (comma-separated user IDs; one for DM, several for group DM), `return_channel` (`true` to get full channel object).
Scope note: the required scope depends on the conversation kind (`im:write` for DMs, `mpim:write` for group DMs, `channels:manage`/`groups:write` for opening an existing channel). If `im:write` is unavailable, find an existing DM instead via `conversations.list '{"types":"im"}'` and match on the `user` field.

**`conversations.create`** — scope `channels:manage` (public) or `groups:write` (private). Params: `name` **required**, `is_private` (`true`). Returns the new `channel`.

**`conversations.invite`** — scope `channels:manage` (public) or `groups:write` (private). Add members: `channel` **required**, `users` **required** (comma-separated IDs, up to ~1,000 per call). Returns the channel; inviting to a private channel requires the inviter to be a member.

**`conversations.rename`** — scope `channels:manage` (public) or `groups:write` (private). `channel` **required**, `name` **required**.

**`conversations.archive`** / **`conversations.unarchive`** — scopes as above. `channel` **required**. Archiving hides the channel from the general list; it is not deletion. Destructive-ish: confirm before running.

**`conversations.setTopic`** / **`conversations.setPurpose`** — scopes as above. `channel` **required**, `topic`/`purpose` **required**.

### Users

**`users.lookupByEmail`** — scope `users:read` (+ `users:read.email` to see the address). `email` **required**. Returns the user object with `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile`.

**`users.info`** — scope `users:read` (+ `users:read.email`). `user` **required** (ID).

**`users.list`** — scope `users:read`. List workspace users. `limit` (default 100, max 200), `cursor`. Returns `members[]`; filter on `is_bot`/`deleted` as needed.

**`users.conversations`** — read scopes by type. List conversations a user (default: the authed user) is in: `user`, `types`, paginated. Slower to page; prefer `conversations.members` per channel when you only need one channel.

### Reactions

**`reactions.add`** — scope `reactions:write`. Params: `channel` **required**, `name` **required** (emoji name without colons, e.g. `+1`), `ts` **required** (target message).

**`reactions.remove`** — scope `reactions:write`. Same params.

**`reactions.get`** — scope `reactions:read`. `channel` **required**, `ts` **required**. Returns `reactions[]` on the message.

**`reactions.list`** — scope `reactions:read`. Reactions by a user (`user`, default authed user), paginated.

### Search

**`search.messages`** — scope `search:read`. Full-text search: `query` **required** (supports operators such as `in:#channel`, `from:@user`, `after:2023-01-01`, quoted phrases). `count` (default 20, max 100). Returns `messages.matches[]`, each with `channel`, `ts`, `user`, `text`, `blocks`.

**`search.files`** / **`search.all`** — scope `search:read`. Same `query` semantics for files or everything at once.

### Files and Uploads

The current upload flow has three steps (the legacy `files.upload` endpoint still exists but should not be used for new work):

1. **`files.getUploadURLExternal`** — scope `files:write`. Params: `filename` **required**, `length` **required** (byte count of the file), `alt_txt`, `snippet_type`. Returns `upload_url` and `file_id`.
2. **PUT** the raw file bytes to `upload_url` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. The upload URL is a temporary, signed, different host — do not POST JSON to it.
3. **`files.completeUploadExternal`** — scope `files:write`. Params: `files` **required** (`[{"id":"F…"}]` from step 1), `channel_id` (to share into a conversation), `initial_comment`, `thread_ts`. Returns `files[]` and, when shared into a channel, the message `channel`/`ts`.

`scripts/upload_file.cjs` automates all three steps from a local path:
```bash
node scripts/upload_file.cjs ./report.pdf C0123456789 --comment "Q3 numbers" --title "Q3 Report"
```
Equivalent raw sequence (for one-off or non-Node environments):
```bash
UP=$(curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"filename\":\"report.pdf\",\"length\":$(stat -f%z report.pdf)}" \
  https://slack.com/api/files.getUploadURLExternal)
# parse upload_url and file_id from UP, then:
curl -s -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @report.pdf "<upload_url>"
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"files":[{"id":"<file_id>"}],"channel_id":"C0123456789","initial_comment":"Q3 numbers"}' \
  https://slack.com/api/files.completeUploadExternal
```
Other file methods: `files.info` (`file`, scope `files:read`), `files.delete` (scope `files:write`, destructive), `files.sharedPublicURL` (scope `files:write`).

### Utility

- **`api.test`** — no token, no auth. Echo test: always callable.
- **`auth.test`** — verifies the token; returns `team`, `team_id`, `user`, `user_id`, `url`, and bot info when applicable.
- **`team.info`** — scope `team:read`. Workspace metadata (`team_id`, `name`, `domain`).
- **`team.billableInfo`** — scope `users:read`/`team:read`; rarely needed.

## Formatting Message Text

Slack uses a lightweight markup called mrkdwn in `text` fields (enabled by default):

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strikethrough~`, `` `code` ``, ``` ``preformatted`` ```, `>quote`
- Mentions: `<@U123456>` (user), `<#C123456>` (channel) — use IDs, not names
- Links: `<https://example.com/page|friendly label>`; bare URLs are linked automatically unless disabled
- Emoji: `:wave:`, `:+1:`, custom workspace emoji also by `:name:`
- Text is limited to 40,000 characters; keep request bodies under ~300 KB

For layout (headers, fields, buttons, dividers, images) use `blocks` (Block Kit) instead of long text:

```json
{
  "channel": "C0123456789",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Deploy finished* in 42s" } },
    { "type": "divider" },
    { "type": "context", "elements": [ { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Run by <@U123456>" } ] }
  ]
}
```

Block reference: `https://api.slack.com/reference/block-kit/blocks`. Interactive elements (buttons, selects) require handling interactive events / `views.open` for modals; static content works everywhere.

## Resolving Names and IDs

Slack Web API methods take encoded IDs; app tokens generally cannot send to a channel by its `#name`. Resolution recipes:

- **Channel by name:** `conversations.list` with `types: "public_channel,private_channel"` and `limit: 200`, page with `--pages`, then match `name === "#general".slice(1)`.
- **DM by user:** `conversations.open '{"users":"U…","return_channel":true}'` → `channel.id` (starts with `D`).
- **User by email:** `users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'` → `user.id` (starts with `U`).
- **Parent message for threads:** take `ts` from the message in `conversations.history` or from the `ts` returned by `chat.postMessage`.

## Pagination

Cursor-based pagination is the norm: responses with more data return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Send it back as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

- `scripts/slack.cjs` follows the cursor automatically when you pass `--pages N` (it merges array results and reports `pagesUsed`).
- Practical per-page `limit` maxima: `conversations.list`/`users.list` 200; `conversations.history` 999; search `count` 100.
- To fetch everything, loop until `next_cursor` is empty — but cap the number of pages to stay inside rate limits (see below).

## Rate Limits

- Slack applies per-method tiers; hitting a limit returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds) and/or `error: "rate_limited"`. Back off for the requested duration before retrying.
- When a method family is over-used, Slack may also throttle with secondary rate-limit headers; slow down rather than hammering.
- Practical guidance: keep polling loops small, cache lookups (channel/user IDs) instead of re-listing, and add small sleeps between bulk operations.
- Tier details live at `https://api.slack.com/docs/rate-limits`; they change, so do not hardcode numeric tiers.

## Error Codes

Every failure response is `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>", ...}` — often with HTTP 200, so always check `ok`. The bundled script prints `Failure: Slack API error: <code>` and exits non-zero. Common codes:

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token rejected | Check the token value; reinstall the app |
| `account_inactive` / `token_revoked` | Token no longer valid | Generate/install a fresh token |
| `missing_scope` | App lacks a scope | Error body includes `needed`; add it to the app and reinstall |
| `no_permission` | Token type not allowed for the action | Use a user token or different app |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad/unknown channel ID | Resolve the ID again via `conversations.list` |
| `not_in_channel` | App/user not a member | `conversations.join`/`invite` first (public) |
| `is_archived` | Channel archived | Unarchive before posting |
| `name_taken` / `invalid_name` | Channel name problem | Pick another name; 1–80 lowercase chars, no spaces |
| `user_not_found` | Bad user ID or not visible to the app | Check `users.lookupByEmail` result |
| `message_too_long` | Text over the limit | Shorten text or move content into `blocks` |
| `invalid_timestamp` | `ts` malformed/unknown | Use the exact `ts` string returned by Slack |
| `already_reacted` / `no_reaction` | Reaction state mismatch | Check current reactions with `reactions.get` |
| `file_not_found` | Bad file ID | Verify `file_id` from the upload step |
| `too_many_requests` / HTTP 429 | Rate limited | Honor `Retry-After`, then retry |
| `internal_error` | Slack-side failure | Retry after a short delay |
| `restricted_action` | Enterprise/org policy blocked it | Adjust org settings or use an admin-approved flow |
| `access_denied` | Org/enterprise policy | Usually requires an admin's approval workflow |

When a call fails, read the full error body: Slack often includes extra context such as `needed`, `provided`, or an `errors` map naming the offending parameter. Official method docs: `https://api.slack.com/methods/<method>`.

# Slack API

## Overview

Enable agent-driven Slack automation against the Slack Web API. All calls are HTTPS requests to `https://slack.com/api/<method>` and return a JSON envelope. Everything below works with `curl` or Python 3 stdlib (`urllib`); no SDK is required, though using one is fine when the environment already provides it.

## Authentication

1. Obtain an OAuth token for a Slack app and keep it out of code:
   - Bot token `xoxb-...` (normal case) in the `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable.
   - User token `xoxp-...` only when the task explicitly requires user-scoped access (e.g., `search.messages`).
2. Send every request with an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
3. Never log, print, or hard-code tokens.

### Response envelope

Every method returns JSON: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success or `{"ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found"}` on failure. Always check `ok` and surface `error` before acting on payload fields.

Sanity-check credentials first:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  https://slack.com/api/auth.test
# -> {"ok":true,"url":"...","team":"...","user":"...","team_id":"T...","user_id":"U..."}
```

## Calling Convention

Minimal Python helper (stdlib only):

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

TOKEN = os.environ["SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"]

def slack(method, **payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"https://slack.com/api/{method}",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
                 "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        return json.load(resp)

result = slack("auth.test")
assert result.get("ok"), result.get("error")
```

Equivalent curl pattern:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from automation"}'
```

## Sending Messages

### Post a message — `chat.postMessage`

Pass `channel` (an ID, never a bare name; see "Resolving Names"), `text`, and optionally `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn`.

```python
r = slack("chat.postMessage",
          channel="C1234567890",
          text="Deploy finished: <https://ci.example.com/build/42|build 42> is green.")
assert r["ok"], r.get("error")
ts = r["ts"]          # message id; store it to update/delete/reply/react later
channel = r["channel"]
```

Success returns `ts` (the message id) and the `channel` the message landed in.

### Reply in a thread

Reuse the parent's `ts` as `thread_ts`. Replies must still target the parent's `channel`:

```python
slack("chat.postMessage",
      channel="C1234567890",
      thread_ts="1614892152.000500",
      text="Adding details to the thread.")
```

### Post ephemeral — `chat.postEphemeral`

Visible only to one user; requires `user` (a `U...` id) plus `channel`:

```python
slack("chat.postEphemeral",
      channel="C1234567890",
      user="U1234567890",
      text="Only you can see this.")
```

### Update / delete — `chat.update`, `chat.delete`

Identify the message by `channel` + `ts` (never by matching text):

```python
slack("chat.update", channel="C1234567890", ts=ts, text="Revised text.")
slack("chat.delete", channel="C1234567890", ts=ts)
```

### Blocks and mrkdwn

Prefer `blocks` for rich messages; `text` still supplies the fallback/notification preview.

- mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, ```preformatted```, `~strike~`.
- Links: `<https://example.com|click here>`.
- Mentions: `<@U1234567890>` for users, `<#C1234567890>` for channels.
- Blocks payload with user mention and formatted text:

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "text": "Build failed",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn",
      "text": "*Build 42 failed* — see <https://ci.example.com/logs/42|logs>. cc <@U1234567890>"}},
    {"type": "divider"},
    {"type": "actions", "elements": [
      {"type": "button", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Retry"},
       "value": "retry_42", "action_id": "retry"}
    ]}
  ]
}
```

Limits: at most 50 blocks; each block `text` field at most 3000 chars; plain `text` at most 40,000 chars. Exceeding them returns `invalid_blocks` or `msg_too_long`.

## Reading Conversations

Prefer the unified `conversations.*` methods over the deprecated `channels.*`, `groups.*`, `im.*`, and `mpim.*` method families (those still exist for legacy read-only edge cases, but are not needed for list/history).

### List conversations — `conversations.list`

Filter with `types` (comma-separated: `public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im`) and pass `exclude_archived=true` unless archives are wanted. Results are paginated — never assume one page returns everything (see Pagination).

```python
def list_conversations(types="public_channel,private_channel"):
    out, cursor = [], ""
    while True:
        page = slack("conversations.list",
                     types=types, exclude_archived=True, limit=200, cursor=cursor)
        assert page["ok"], page.get("error")
        out += page["channels"]
        cursor = (page.get("response_metadata") or {}).get("next_cursor", "")
        if not cursor:
            return out
```

### Open a DM or private channel — `conversations.open`

`conversations.open` with `users` (comma-separated user ids for a DM) returns the conversation `channel.id` (`D...` for a 1:1 DM). Posting to a DM channel without first opening it fails.

### Read history — `conversations.history`

`channel` is required; `limit` (1–999), `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` are epoch-seconds (or message `ts`) filters, `inclusive` controls whether the boundary message is included. Returns newest-first `messages`.

```python
page = slack("conversations.history", channel="C1234567890", limit=100)
assert page["ok"], page.get("error")
for m in page["messages"]:
    print(m.get("ts"), m.get("user"), m.get("text"))
```

### Read a thread — `conversations.replies`

Pass `channel` and the parent `ts` to fetch the whole thread including the parent message.

### Resolving Names to IDs

Use IDs everywhere in API calls; resolve a human-supplied channel/user name only when necessary:

1. Channel name → ID: paginate `conversations.list` with `types=public_channel,private_channel` and match `name` (case-insensitive). Prefix `#` from the user input is not part of `name`.
2. User → ID: `users.lookupByEmail` when an email is known; otherwise paginate `users.list` and match `name` or `profile.display_name`.
3. If the ID is not found, report `channel_not_found` / `user_not_found` style errors instead of guessing.

## Users

- `users.list` — paginated (limit up to 200); each member has `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.display_name`, `profile.email` (email only when the `users:read.email` scope is present).
- `users.lookupByEmail` — fastest way to map an email to a `U...` id; requires `users:read.email`.
- `users.info` — one user by `user` id.

## Uploading Files

`files.upload` is deprecated (removal planned for 2025); use the two-step upload API:

1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename`, `length` (byte count), optional `alt_txt`, `snippet_type` → returns `upload_url` and `file_id`.
2. `PUT` the raw file bytes to `upload_url` (no Slack auth header required on this URL).
3. `files.completeUploadExternal` with `files: [{"id": file_id, "title": filename}]` → returns the `file` object. Pass `channel_id` (and optional `thread_ts`) on this final call to share the file into a conversation.

```python
import os, urllib.request

data = open("report.pdf", "rb").read()
meta = slack("files.getUploadURLExternal",
             filename="report.pdf", length=len(data), alt_txt="Monthly report")
assert meta["ok"], meta.get("error")

put = urllib.request.Request(meta["upload_url"], data=data, method="PUT")
with urllib.request.urlopen(put) as resp:
    assert resp.status in (200, 201), resp.status

done = slack("files.completeUploadExternal",
             files=[{"id": meta["file_id"], "title": "report.pdf"}],
             channel_id="C1234567890")
assert done["ok"], done.get("error")
```

## Reactions

```python
slack("reactions.add", channel="C1234567890", name="white_check_mark", timestamp=ts)
slack("reactions.remove", channel="C1234567890", name="x", timestamp=ts)
```

Pass emoji names without surrounding colons. To react inside a thread, `timestamp` is the target message's `ts`.

## Search

`search.messages` is the only practical way to search across channels, but bot tokens are not granted the `search:read` scope — it requires a user token (`xoxp-...`). If only a bot token is available, say so rather than pretending search works, and offer to scan specific channels with `conversations.history` instead.

## Pagination Pattern

List-style methods (`conversations.list`, `conversations.history`, `users.list`, `search.messages`, ...) page with `cursor` + `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Loop until `next_cursor` is empty or absent; never assume the first page is the whole result.

```python
def paginate(method, items_key, **params):
    params.setdefault("limit", 200)
    params.setdefault("cursor", "")
    while True:
        page = slack(method, **params)
        assert page["ok"], page.get("error")
        for item in page.get(items_key, []):
            yield item
        nxt = (page.get("response_metadata") or {}).get("next_cursor", "")
        if not nxt:
            break
        params["cursor"] = nxt

channels = list(paginate("conversations.list", "channels",
                         types="public_channel", exclude_archived=True))
```

## Errors, Rate Limits, and Retries

- `ok: false` responses carry a machine-readable `error`. Common codes:

  | error | meaning / fix |
  |---|---|
  | `not_authed`, `invalid_auth`, `account_inactive`, `token_revoked` | token missing, wrong, or disabled |
  | `missing_scope`, `no_permission`, `restricted_action` | app lacks the scope/permission for this method |
  | `channel_not_found` | unknown channel id, or the app is not a member of a private channel |
  | `user_not_found` | unknown user id |
  | `is_archived` | target channel is archived |
  | `name_taken` | conversation name already in use |
  | `msg_too_long`, `invalid_blocks` | payload exceeds message limits |
  | `ratelimited`, HTTP 429 | slow down; obey `Retry-After` |
  | `internal_error`, HTTP 5xx | transient; retry with backoff |

- On HTTP 429 read the `Retry-After` header (seconds) and wait that long before retrying.
- On HTTP 5xx or network failure, retry with exponential backoff and jitter (e.g., 1s, 2s, 4s... capped).
- Be careful retrying writes: a timed-out `chat.postMessage` may still have been delivered, so a blind retry can duplicate a message. If a write times out without a response, prefer verifying via history or reporting the uncertainty over immediate re-send.

## Scopes and Token Setup

Create an app at `https://api.slack.com/apps` → OAuth & Permissions → add Bot Token Scopes → Install to Workspace → copy the Bot User OAuth Token (`xoxb-...`) into `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`.

Common bot scopes:

- `chat:write` — send/update/delete messages, ephemeral messages, threads.
- `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` — read message history in each conversation type.
- `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`, `channels:manage` — conversation metadata; create/archive/manage.
- `users:read`, `users:read.email` — list users and read emails.
- `files:write`, `files:read` — upload and read files.
- `reactions:write`, `reactions:read` — add/remove/read reactions.
- `team:read` — workspace metadata when needed.

## Working Guidelines

- Always address conversations, users, and messages by ID (`C...`, `D...`, `G...`, `U...`, `ts`). Resolve human-supplied names once, then reuse the IDs.
- Always paginate list endpoints; one page is not the full dataset.
- Use `conversations.*` methods; avoid deprecated legacy methods (`channels.list`, `im.list`, ...) unless a task explicitly requires them.
- The app must be a member of a private channel to read or post to it (`conversations.join` covers public channels only; for private ones the app must be invited or added via `conversations.invite` with `channels:manage`).
- Posting to a DM usually requires `conversations.open` first.
- Treat `ts` values as opaque message ids (strings like `"1614892152.000500"`). For `oldest`/`latest` filters you may pass the `ts` string or epoch-seconds (float or string).
- Sending to an archived channel fails with `is_archived`; tell the user and ask before unarchiving.
- If a request needs a scope the configured token lacks, report the exact `missing_scope` error and the scope name; do not silently degrade.
